title: Orphée
format: Softcover, Swiss binding, metallic mirrored cover

description.main: Younès Klouche's first book revisits the North American sites of the 1975 New Topographics exhibition and assembles 26 unstaged black-and-white photographs into a fictional territory. The title and the book's play of mirrors, inside the pictures and on its metallic cover, come from Jean Cocteau's 1950 film Orphée. Published by Éditions du LIC in 2016 in an edition of 500.
description.extended:
Younès Klouche's first book, Orphée, revisits the North American sites of the 1975 New Topographics exhibition and rebuilds them as a place that does not exist.

The 26 black-and-white plates show suburban houses, parked cars, office towers and the spaces between them. None is staged, so each reads as reportage. In sequence they form a fiction made from fragments of American reality. The title comes from Jean Cocteau's 1950 film, in which mirrors are the passage to death. Mirroring runs through the object as well as the pictures: chrome and glass inside the frames, a mirrored metallic cover, facing pages that answer one another as they turn. Éditions du LIC published the book in 2016 as a Swiss-bound softcover of 48 pages, 23 by 33 cm, in an edition of 500, long out of print.

Klouche, born in Lausanne, graduated from ECAL in 2015 and began the work as a student there. He spent more than a year on the sequence before Éditions du LIC proposed the book. He now works between Lausanne and Paris as a photographer and director. His later study of the Paris periphery, Panamera, was first shown at the 2022 Swiss Design Awards in Basel.
description.artist_bio: Younès Klouche (b. Lausanne) graduated with honours from ECAL in 2015. Photographer and director based in Paris and Lausanne, represented by Obvious; commercial still-life work for Dior, Hublot, Nike, Omega and others; personal projects shown at the Musée de l'Elysée and Tate Modern. Panamera (2022), a three-year study of the Paris periphery, shown at Art Basel / Swiss Design Awards and the Swiss Embassy in Seoul.

notes: Shelf: Mixed. First edition, edition of 500; 26 plates; Swiss-bound metallic softcover. Éditions du LIC later released a small number of archive copies (listed as Orphée Archival Copy).
